column2: Enjoyed by cattle, poured by the unyoked; may we follow after you, Indra and Vishnu; dwelling on the back of heaven, may they rejoice here in Vishnu's world.

Bhuh: food for Agni and Earth, svaha. Bhuvah: food for Vayu and the Air, svaha. Svah: food for Aditya and Heaven, svaha. Bhur Bhuvah Svah: food for the Moon and the Directions, svaha. Homage to the gods; svadha to the fathers. Bhur Bhuvah Svah: food. Om.

Bhuh to Agni and Earth, svaha. Bhuvah to Vayu and the Air, svaha. Svah to Aditya and Heaven, svaha. Bhur Bhuvah Svah to the Moon and the Directions, svaha. Homage to the gods; svadha to the fathers. Bhur Bhuvah Svah, Agni. Om.

Bhuh to Agni and Earth and the Great, svaha. Bhuvah to Vayu and the Air and the Great, svaha. Svah to Aditya and Heaven and the Great, svaha. Bhur Bhuvah Svah to the Moon, the Stars, the Directions and the Great, svaha. Homage to the gods; svadha to the fathers. Bhur Bhuvah Svah Mahah. Om.
Protect us from sin, Agni, svaha. Protect us, all-knowing, svaha. Protect the sacrifice, shining one, svaha. Protect all, hundred-powered, svaha.
Protect us, Agni, with one; protect with a second; protect with strength with a third; protect with four songs, O Vasu, svaha.

He who is the bull of the meters, of all forms, who entered the meters from the meters; the Upanishad spoken by Indra, the eldest, for strength to the seers. Homage to the gods; svadha to the fathers. Bhur Bhuvah Svah, the meter. Om.
Homage to Brahman. May I have retention without rejection; may I be a holder of what is heard by my ears; may what I have heard not depart from me. Om.

Truth is austerity; reality is austerity; learning is austerity; peace is austerity; self-control is austerity; calm is austerity; giving is austerity; sacrifice is austerity. Bhur Bhuvah Svah: worship Brahman; this is austerity.

As the fragrance of a flowering tree is carried by the wind from afar, so the fragrance of a virtuous deed is carried from afar. As one who walks on a sword's edge over a pit — "If I fall, I shall call out again and again" — so one should guard oneself from the immortal.
Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the Self is set in the cave of this creature. The sorrowless sees him, the actionless, by the grace of the Creator, his greatness, the Lord.
From him the seven breaths are born, seven flames, seven fuels, seven tongues; these seven worlds in which move the breaths dwelling in the cave, set seven and seven.
From him come all oceans and mountains; from him flow the rivers of all forms; from him all plants and juices, by which this inner Self stays as the element.
Brahma of the gods, the leader of seers, the sage of the wise, the buffalo of beasts, the falcon of vultures, the axe of woods — Soma crosses the filter roaring.
The one unborn female, red, white and black, producing many offspring of like form; one unborn male lies enjoying her; another unborn abandons her, whose enjoyment is finished.

The swan dwelling in purity, the Vasu in the air, the priest at the altar, the guest in the house; dwelling among men, in the best, in truth, in the sky, born of water, of cattle, of truth, of mountain — the great truth.

From whom none higher was born, who entered all the worlds; Prajapati, agreeing with creatures, joins the three lights; he is the sixteenfold. We call the sustainer, who gives us wealth, Savitar who watches men. They wish to sprinkle ghee; ghee is his womb, in ghee he rests, ghee is his abode; bring in due order, be glad, bull; carry the offering offered with svaha.
From the ocean the honeyed wave rose up; with the drop it attained immortality. The secret name of ghee is the tongue of the gods, the navel of immortality.
We shall proclaim the name; with ghee at this sacrifice we hold it with homage; let Brahma hear the praise; the four-horned bull bellowed.
Four horns, three feet, two heads, seven hands has he; bound in three ways, the bull roars; the great god has entered mortals.
Placed threefold, hidden by the Panis, the gods found ghee in the cow; Indra produced one, Surya one; from Vena they fashioned one by their own power.
Who first of the gods, before them, higher than all, Rudra, the great sage — see Hiranyagarbha being born; may that god unite us with good understanding.
Than whom there is nothing higher or lower, than whom no one is subtler or greater; standing alone in heaven like a tree, by that Person all this is filled.
Not by work, not by offspring, not by wealth, but by renunciation some attained immortality; the heaven set beyond in the cave shines, which the strivers enter.

Those whose meaning is ascertained by the knowledge of Vedanta, the ascetics of pure sattva through the yoga of renunciation, in Brahma's world at the supreme end of time are freed, all of them supreme immortals.
The small, sinless, supreme, stone-like lotus set in the midst of the city; in it too a small space, free of sorrow; what is within that is to be worshipped.
The sound declared at the beginning of the Veda and established at the end of the Veda; beyond it that is dissolved in nature is the Great Lord.
The thousand-headed god, all-eyed, source of the universe; the universe, the god Narayana, the imperishable, the supreme lord.
Supreme on all sides, eternal, the universe, Narayana Hari; the Person is indeed all this, and the universe lives on him.
Lord of the universe, Lord of the Self, eternal, auspicious, undying; Narayana, the great one to be known, Self of the universe, the supreme refuge.
Narayana is supreme Brahman; Narayana is the supreme truth; Narayana is the supreme light; Narayana is the supreme Self.
Infinite, imperishable, the seer, at the end in the ocean, source of the universe; the heart too resembling a lotus bud, facing downward.
It stands a span below the throat and above the navel; know that heart as the great abode of the universe.
Spread with veins it hangs like a bud; at its end is a subtle hollow, in which all is established.
In its middle is a great fire, universal in flame, facing all sides; it eats first, distributing, standing, an ageless seer who takes food.
Lying across, above and below, its rays are spread; it heats its own body from foot to head. In its middle a fire-flame, subtler than the subtle, is established upright.
Standing in the middle of a blue cloud, bright like a line of lightning; slender like a grain-awn of wild rice, yellow, luminous, atom-like.
In the middle of that flame the Supreme Self is established. He is Brahma, he is Shiva, he is Hari, with Indra; he is the imperishable, the supreme, the self-luminous.

This Aditya indeed heats this orb; there those are the verses; the orb is by verses; it is the world of verses. Then the flame that shines in this orb — those are the Saman chants; it is the world of the chants. Then the Person in the flame of this orb — those are the Yajus formulas; the orb is by the Yajus; it is the world of the Yajus. This is the threefold knowledge itself that shines, the golden Person who is within the sun.

The sun is radiance, vigor, strength, fame, eye, ear, self, mind, wrath, Manu, death, truth, Mitra, wind, space, breath, guardian of the world; Ka, what, which, that truth, food, the immortal, life, the universe; which one, the self-existent Brahman, this immortal. This is the Person, lord of beings; he who knows thus attains union with Brahma, sameness of world, and union, equality of rank and same world with these deities — thus the Upanishad.
They worship the shining Sun, Aditya; austerity and truth, the honey flows; that Brahman, that waters, water, light, essence, immortality, Brahman; Bhur Bhuvah Svah. Om.

Homage to the lord of death. Homage to the one who ends the fall of death. Homage to the upward one. Homage to the upward-marked. Homage to the golden. Homage to the golden-marked. Homage to the fair-colored. Homage to the fair-colored-marked. Homage to the divine. Homage to the divine-marked. Homage to Bhava. Homage to Bhava-marked. Homage to Sharva. Homage to Sharva-marked. Homage to Shiva. Homage to Shiva-marked. Homage to the blazing. Homage to the blazing-marked. Homage to the Self. Homage to the Self-marked. Homage to the supreme. Homage to the supreme-marked. This establishes the all-marked, of Soma and the Sun, the hand-formula, the purifier.
I take refuge in Sadyojata; homage, homage to Sadyojata. In birth after birth may you not carry me beyond birth; be mine. Homage to the source of existence.

Homage to Vamadeva, homage to the eldest, homage to the best, homage to Rudra, homage to Time, homage to the tamer of time, homage to the tamer of strength, homage to strength, homage to the crusher of strength, homage to the subduer of all beings, homage to the one who raises the mind.
To the non-terrible, and the terrible, and the more than terrible; on all sides, Sharva, to all, homage be to you in your Rudra forms.
We know the Person; we meditate on Mahadeva; may Rudra urge us on that.
Ishana, lord of all knowledges, Lord of all beings, lord of Brahman, lord of the Brahman, Brahma, Shiva — may he be mine, Sadashiva. Om.
Homage to the golden-armed, golden-colored, golden-formed, lord of gold; to the lord of Ambika, lord of Uma, lord of beasts, homage, homage.
Truth, reality, the supreme Brahman, the Person, dark-tawny, of upward seed, of strange eyes — homage, homage to him of universal form.

All is Rudra; homage to that Rudra. The Person is Rudra, great being; homage, homage. The universe, being, world, the wondrous, born in many ways and being born — all this is Rudra; homage to that Rudra.
To the wise Rudra, the most bountiful, the strong, may we speak a most blessed word from the heart. All this is Rudra; homage to that Rudra.
The Vaikankata ladle of whose Agnihotra is such, his offerings stand opposite and firm, for establishment.

Five verses beginning "Make your might": Make your might like a spreading net; go forth like a king with followers on an elephant; pursuing the net, wasting, you hurl, pierce the demons with your hottest.
Your swift whirlings fall; touch boldly, blazing; Agni, with the ladle consume the flying ones; unfettered, release the fire-brands in all directions.
Release your touches; be swiftest; be the guard of this clan, unharmed; whoever at a distance or near plans harm to us, Agni, let none of them harm you.
Arise, Agni; spread against; burn down the foes, sharp-armed. Whoever, kindled, makes an enemy for us, burn him down like dry grass.
Be upright; look toward us; reveal the divine things, Agni; loosen the firm ones of the sorcerers; destroy the kin and non-kin, the foes.

Aditi, gods, Gandharvas, men, fathers, Asuras — of all these beings the mother, the Earth, great, Mahi, Savitri, Gayatri, Jagati, wide Prithvi, abundant, universal; which body is that? She is truth, she is immortality — thus said Vasishtha.

The waters are indeed all this, all beings; waters are breath; waters are cattle; waters are food; waters are immortality; waters are the sovereign, Viraj, Svaraj; waters are the meters; waters are the lights; waters are the Yajus; waters are truth; waters are all deities; waters: Bhur Bhuvah Svah. Om.
May the waters purify the earth; may the purified earth purify me; may Brahmanaspati purify; may the Brahman-purified purify me.
Whatever remnant, uneatable, or ill-conduct is mine, may the waters purify all of it, and the accepting of gifts from the wicked, svaha.

May Agni and Wrath and the lords of wrath protect me from the sins done by wrath. Whatever sin I have committed in the day, by mind, speech, hands, feet, belly, or organ — may the day efface it. Whatever evil is in me, this I offer, myself, to the source of immortality, in truth, in light, svaha.

May the Sun and Wrath and the lords of wrath protect me from the sins done by wrath. Whatever sin I have committed in the night, by mind, speech, hands, feet, belly, or organ — may the night efface it. Whatever evil is in me, this I offer, myself, to the source of immortality, in the Sun, in light, svaha.
Om is the one-syllable Brahman. Agni is the deity; Brahman — thus the seer. The Gayatri meter; the form is the Supreme Self; the application is for union.
Come, boon-giving goddess, the imperishable, equal to Brahman; Gayatri, mother of the meters, accept this prayer of ours.
Whatever sin one commits by day, from that by day he is freed; whatever sin one commits by night, from that by night he is freed. O great goddess of all colors, Sandhya-vidya, Sarasvati.

You are vigor, you are might, you are strength, you are radiance, you are the abodes and names of the gods; you are the universe, all life, all, all-living, the overcoming. Om. I invoke Gayatri, I invoke Savitri, I invoke Sarasvati, I invoke the meters, I invoke Shri. Of Gayatri, the meter Gayatri, the seer Vishvamitra, the deity Savitar; Agni the mouth, Brahma the head, Vishnu the heart, Rudra the topknot, earth the source; with prana, apana, vyana, udana and samana; white-colored, of the Sankhyayana gotra; Gayatri of twenty-four syllables, three feet, six bellies, five heads; application at initiation.

Om Bhuh. Om Bhuvah. Om Svah. Om Mahah. Om Janah. Om Tapah. Om Satyam. Om, we meditate on the choicest radiance of the god Savitar; may he urge on our thoughts. Om, the waters, the light, the essence, immortality, Brahman; Bhur Bhuvah Svah. Om.
O goddess, on the highest peak, born on the earth at the mountain's head, permitted by the Brahmins, go, goddess, as you wish.
Praised by me, the boon-giving mother of the Veda, urging the twice-born in the wind, having given me life on earth, wealth, and Brahmanical splendor, go to Brahma's world.
